text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. When developers write new code, they regularly add it to a shared project. Each time this happens, automated builds start automatically, so the team does not need to build the software by hand. During these builds, the system runs tests to check that everything still works correctly. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious problems. A CI pipeline usually includes several steps, such as building, testing, and reporting results. Thanks to these pipelines, developers receive fast feedback and can fix mistakes quickly, which makes the whole development process smoother and more reliable.
